cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: What Aren’t You Saying?
cards.instruction: Find out what someone is holding back by treating every careful answer as incomplete.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. You called my audition interesting. What came after that in your head?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're my sister. I'm trying to be encouraging.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Then give me the encouraging half and the half you swallowed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your singing was better than your dancing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Better by how much? Are we buying dance lessons or shoes that don't move?

mechanism: A treats a sibling carefully encouraging feedback as an incomplete report and authorizes bluntness before demanding a usable degree of criticism.
confusable: D99 seeks understanding of hurt; D102 probes what a careful answer conceals rather than explaining A feelings.
comparison: Audition singing/dancing feedback differs from omissions in proposal minutes requiring a signature.
seedUse: Use D102-a encouraging half and relative dancing assessment, with A controlling acceptable completeness rather than adding a rank slogan.
